text:
jen_ml: FYI — we pushed the nodes to driver 535.86 this morning and CIs are showing a 30-40% regression on tail latency for small-batch chat workloads. nsys traces look weird: lots of CUDA API stalls and CUPTI warnings. Anyone seen CUPTI + nsys act up after a driver bump?

tim_infra: saw something similar last month with 535.x on a different cluster. CUPTI metadata reads were failing for some kernels, caused nsys to mis-time kernels. Do you have the nsys CLI output? :eyes: 

jen_ml: pasted the minimal nsys capture + stderr we got:
```
$ nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --stats=true -o /tmp/trace ./redwood-runtime --config small-batch
CUPTI ERROR: cuptiActivityEnable failed (1)
Warning: CUPTI: activity buffer overflow
...
API calls look serialized:
cudaLaunchKernel(...)	start 0.123s	end 0.456s
cudaMemcpyAsync(...)	start 0.457s	end 0.459s

nsys reported hotspots: many tiny kernels back-to-back instead of overlapping on different SMs.
```

matt_r: quick checklist: which nsys version? Which CUDA/CUPTI path does the profiler pick up? nsys <-> driver mismatches are common. Also, are you running as root or via k8s non-root? Permissions can make CUPTI fail.

jen_ml: using nsight-sys 2024.1.0 (nsys 2024.1) and CUDA 12.2 on AMIs. Ran on k8s daemonset non-root. Pod logs show `CUPTI: Cannot access device` intermittently.

sara_ops: non-root + newer driver rings a bell. On our on-prem we had to bind-mount /dev/nvidia* and /proc/driver/nvidia into the pod and set CAP_SYS_ADMIN for the profiling job. Otherwise CUPTI attaches fail. But the buffering overflow is odd.

carla: also check LD_LIBRARY_PATH picking up an old libcupti.so from system vs container. We had a mismatch where container had CUDA 12.1 libs but host driver was newer — nsys attached to host CUPTI path and got inconsistent symbol sizes.

matt_r: exactly. I recommend: 1) run `nsys env` inside the pod to see what CUPTI path it uses; 2) try nsys 2023.12 if you must profile against driver 535.x — 2024.1 introduced a change in CUPTI sampling that regresses on some 535 drivers.

jen_ml: tried `nsys env` — it points at `/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` inside container (CUDA 12.2). Host /usr/lib64 has a different libcupti -> mismatch. Is that enough to explain kernel serialization?

tim_infra: yep. If CUPTI cannot read activity attributes correctly it will misreport duration and ordering. That can make us misdiagnose batching heuristics as broken when it's actually profiling artifacts. Also check kernel timestamps in raw perfetto timeline vs nsys. If perfetto (without CUPTI) shows overlap but nsys doesn't, it's a CUPTI/driver issue.

jen_ml: good point. I ran perfetto on the node (ftrace + perf events) and it shows kernels overlapping. So runtime likely fine, profiler broken. But still seeing perf regressions in prod — could be unrelated but coincident with the driver bump.

carla: two more things: 1) driver 535.86 had a reported bug where `cuptiActivityGetKind` returned wrong sizes for inline PTX kernels causing buffer overflows; NVIDIA ticket said workaround is to force `CUPTI_DISABLE_ACTIVITY_KIND=...` for certain activities. 2) nsys has `--sample-funcs` vs activity-mode differences — try switching modes.

matt_r: workaround we used: downgrade driver to 525.85 (stable for our stack) or pin nsys to 2023.12. For ephemeral profiling jobs, run them as root with device file mounts and explicit CUPTI path: `export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` and `export CUPTI_LIB=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64`. That fixed attach errors for us.

jen_ml: can you paste the exact `nsys profile` incantation that worked? I want to re-run with the same flags and compare timelines.

matt_r: sure — this is what we used to get correct activity-based timelines on 525 driver:
```
export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output /tmp/trace_fixed \
  --sample=cpu --stats=true ./redwood-runtime --config small-batch
```
We also increased CUPTI buffer sizes by setting `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND` env to limit collection to `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL` only for short captures.

sara_ops: from infra side, if you want to profile on k8s pods without dangerous caps we have a profiling job that mounts `--device=/dev/nvidia0` and `hostPath: /usr/lib64/libcuda.so` and runs as root in a separate nodepool. I can spin one up for you.

jen_ml: please do. Also noticed the runtime's batching heuristic starts breaking when KV cache hits drop below ~85% (micro-bench). Could the driver change affect memory access patterns and cause more KV evictions, making smaller batches and higher overhead?

tim_infra: unlikely driver changes randomize eviction counts, but if GPU memory bookkeeping changed (different allocation behavior) it could increase fragmentation and cause earlier evictions. Check our KV cache logs + tuning: enable `KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1` and capture allocation timeline.

carla: Another quick profiler tip: use `nvprof --profile-from-start off` for a narrow window around a request to avoid long-running CUPTI overflows. nvprof is deprecated but sometimes more tolerant on weird driver combos.

gpu-bot: [automated] Created infra profiling job #pf-402 for jen_ml on nodepool-profilers (driver pinned to 525.85). Logs will appear in #eng-runtime-profiling. :white_check_mark:

jen_ml: awesome, thanks. Plan: run the same micro-bench with pinned driver and nsys 2023.12, capture nsys+perfetto, and compare KV cache allocation traces. Will report back with timelines and a short kernel list. If we still see regressions after confirming profiler artifacts, we'll open an incident.

matt_r: one last note — if you need raw kernel names and SASS hotspots run `cuobjdump --dump-sass` on the model lib and compare to nsys kernel names. Sometimes JIT/ptx->sass changes cause different kernel variants to be picked and perf to change.

jen_ml: noted. thanks everyone. tagging @tim_infra for help with mounting & nodepool.

tim_infra: on it. I'll attach the profiling node and share SSH when ready. :)
